timezone_note: Publish times are UTC. 16:00, 19:00, 22:00 and 01:00 UTC are noon, 3pm, 6pm and 9pm US Eastern (EDT).

formats.label: True fact that sounds fake
formats.brief: One real, well-documented fact that sounds made up (history, science, nature, the human body, space). Only use facts you are highly confident are true and that appear in mainstream reference sources. No rumours, no disputed statistics, no 'scientists say' without a specific finding. Build up to the most surprising detail and save it for the last line.

formats.label: 40-second twist story
formats.brief: An original, short, first-person fictional story (creepy, eerie or mind-bending, never gory) with a twist in the final line that recontextualises everything. The last line should make the viewer want to rewatch from the start.

formats.label: Impossible choice
formats.brief: A genuinely hard 'what would you do' dilemma or 'would you rather' with real stakes on both sides. Lay out option A and option B vividly, add one complication halfway through that makes it harder, and end by asking the viewer to pick A or B in the comments. Both sides must feel defensible so people argue.

formats.label: The Last Signal teaser
formats.brief: A self-contained eerie micro-scene from the fictional series The Last Signal: a coastal city built over a forgotten military installation, where a buried transmission from the past starts reaching people in the present. Use one concrete clue (a log entry, a recording, a number station, a missing person). End on an unresolved, chilling question that makes people want the full story on the channel.
